subject: Math
prompt:
[Table 1]

Two investments were made as shown in the table above. The interest in Account X is compounded once per year. Which of the following is true about the investments?

choices.A: Account X always earns more money per year than Account Y.
choices.B: Account X always earns less money per year than Account Y.
choices.C: Account X earns more money per year than Account Y at first but eventually earns less money per year.
choices.D: Account X earns less money per year than Account Y at first but eventually earns more money per year.

explanation: Choice A is correct. Account X starts with $$800$ and earns interest at $5\%$ per year, so in the first year Account X earns $(800)(0.05) =$ $$40$, which is greater than the $$35$ that Account Y earns that year. Compounding interest can be modeled by an increasing exponential function, so each year Account X will earn more money than it did the previous year. Therefore, each year Account X earns at least $$40$ in interest. Since Account Y always earns $$35$ each year, Account X always earns more money per year than Account Y.
